messages:
matt: quick one — i'm seeing nsys captures for shortburst inference runs drop a bunch of kernels around the KV-prefetch -> attention handoff. i'm running with --trace=cuda,nvtx,osrt and a 200ms capture window. any common pitfalls?

laura: yup, that's a very common symptom. short capture windows + OSRT sampling can misalign and miss lightweight kernels. two quick paths: expand the capture window to include warmup+steady state, or bracket the capture exactly around the critical code path.

laura: try this pattern first (bash):
```
nsys profile \
  --trace=cuda,nvtx,osrt \
  --capture-range=manual \
  --capture-range-start=0 \
  --capture-range-duration=1000 \
  --output=shortburst_capture
```
that gives a 1s window — still short but covers warmup for most shortburst runs.

sophia: also add NVTX markers around the batch/kvcache handoff so you can filter easily in the timeline. small python snippet:
```python
import nvtx
for i, batch in enumerate(batches):
    nvtx.range_push(f"prefetch_{i}")
    kv_prefetch(batch)
    nvtx.range_pop()

    nvtx.range_push(f"atten_{i}")
    run_attention(batch)
    nvtx.range_pop()
```
makes it trivial to see if the kernel gap is real or a sampling artifact.

laura: another trick — run several short captures with slight offsets and then compare. sampling noise will move but real kernel omissions persist. also bump OSRT sampling rate if you can (reduces chance of missing micro-kernels). if you're stuck on CLI flags we usually use a pattern like:
```
nsys profile --trace=cuda,nvtx,osrt --output=runX --capture-range=manual --capture-range-duration=1200
# repeat 6 times with 50ms offsets
```

matt: good tips. any infra-level things? i'm seeing more gaps when the process isn't pinned.

sophia: yep — CPU scheduling jitter and GPU preemption can move OSRT samples. pin the serving process to a small set of cores during capture:
```
taskset -c 4-7 python -m serve.entrypoint
```
also isolate noisy daemons (disable background cron/backup on the node if possible).

laura: final thing — if you suspect kernel selection switching (quantized vs fp kernels) add a config toggle to force a single kernel path and reproduce. if the gap disappears it's likely a kernel-switch/regression, not nsys sampling.

matt: i will try bracketed 1s windows + nvtx + core pinning and post back. thanks. :thumbsup:

eng-ci-bot: matt's capture (3901239012) completed with tags [nsys, shortburst, debug] — created artifact shortburst_capture.qdrep (uploaded to ci-artifacts).

matt: confirmed — after NVTX and 1s brackets the gap is reproducible and points to a tiny kernel that only runs when kv-prefetch hits. filing a perf regression ticket with kernel timeline screenshot.
